This is handled in the case of removing the joint with:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d53a62898a65ba635efd554b101e033070c784c/scene/3d/physics/joints/joint_3d.cpp#L53-L57

I think this is something that needs to be documented better as I suspect the behavior is intentional to improve performance when operating on servers directly

> This is handled in the case of removing the joint with:
> 
> [godot/scene/3d/physics/joints/joint_3d.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2d53a62898a65ba635efd554b101e033070c784c/scene/3d/physics/joints/joint_3d.cpp#L53-L57)
> 
> Lines 53 to 57 in [2d53a62](/godotengine/godot/commit/2d53a62898a65ba635efd554b101e033070c784c)
>  void Joint3D::_update_joint(bool p_only_free) { 
>  	if (ba.is_valid() && bb.is_valid()) { 
>  		PhysicsServer3D::get_singleton()->body_remove_collision_exception(ba, bb); 
>  		PhysicsServer3D::get_singleton()->body_remove_collision_exception(bb, ba); 
>  	} 
> 
> I think this is something that needs to be documented better as I suspect the behavior is intentional to improve performance when operating on servers directly

Did some more investigation. It seems like `joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies` is simply a shortcut for adding two exceptions between:
- body A and body B
- body B and body A

That is, calling `joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies` with `true` is equivalent to calling `body_add_collision_exception` two times, and calling `joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies` with `false` is equivalent to calling `body_remove_collision_exception` two times.

So any combination of these can also be used to cancel each other out. For example:
```
PhysicsServer3D.joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies(a, b, true)
PhysicsServer3D.body_remove_collision_exception(a, b)
PhysicsServer3D.body_remove_collision_exception(b, a)
```
is equivalent to:
```
PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception(a, b)
PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception(b, a)
PhysicsServer3D.joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies(a, b, false)
```

If this is intentional, the docs need to clarify a few things:
- `PhysicsServer3D.joint_disable_collisions_between_bodies` is not a joint-scope operation at all.
- `PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception` is not a symmetrical operation.
- Deleting a `Joint3D` that has `Exclude Nodes From Collision` enabled will remove any collision exceptions added outside of the context of that `Joint3D` node.
Those are all great observations and sounds like something to document

I think this behavior should be taken to a totally separate thing from `body_add_collision_exception`. Right now there is a problem between 2D and 3D physics:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/070dc9897ea1b84ab2a7ec04b9bc1b94f38a0eaf/scene/3d/physics/joints/joint_3d.cpp#L56-L60

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/070dc9897ea1b84ab2a7ec04b9bc1b94f38a0eaf/scene/2d/physics/joints/joint_2d.cpp#L58-L61

Notice the different checks of `exclude_from_collision`. But that's not even the real problem with the current approach. I'm facing an issue right now related to this. I have two joints that connect the same two bodies, one of them enables collision exception, the other does not. Here is an example:

1. Some script code that creates a joint:
    1. script adds an collision exceptions between A and B on PhysicsServer3D
    2. script creates Joint Y that connects C and D, and sets `exclude_from_collision` to false (we already set the exclusions up, no need for the joint to care)
2. Joints in the scene file:
    1. Joint X (node A, node B): ignore enabled
    2. Joint Z (node A, node B): ignore disabled

There are problems all over with the current implementation.
1. Order of the joints in the scene tree affect the resulting exceptions.
2. It matters where in the script the exception is set, as it could be before or after the joints configure, and before or after the new joint is added to the scene tree.
3. Changing the nodes that a joint manages will always clear exceptions in 3D, but only if the exception bool is `true` in 2D. Whatever the approach is, both may not be desired by a developer if they have manually scripted an exception at any time.

The joints should only track their exception boolean, never calling `body_add_collision_exception` or `body_remove_collision_exception`. Then, when deciding if two bodies can collide:
1. Check if an exception exists as set by `body_add_collision_exception`
2. If no exception is found, checks the joints of each body. `jolt_joint_3d` already has bodies remembering what joints they are part of:
    https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/070dc9897ea1b84ab2a7ec04b9bc1b94f38a0eaf/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_body_3d.cpp#L1057-L1061
3. If any joints have `exclude_from_collision`, then the bodies don't collide
4. If no joints could be found with the flag enabled, the bodies will collide

This way, joints will not interfere with manually applied exceptions, and having multiple joints on a body won't break exceptions if you delete only one of them, even if it had `exclude_from_collision` set to `true`, because they never set or clear things by themselves.

Another problem I see, at least on the Jolt module side, exceptions are not stored in a Set, they are a Vector, meaning the result of the calls:
```gdscript
PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception(A, B)
PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception(A, B)
# Body A now has B listed twice
PhysicsServer3D.body_remove_collision_exception(A, B)
# Body A now has B listed once
```
These methods should be fixed to only allow one copy of an exception at a time:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/070dc9897ea1b84ab2a7ec04b9bc1b94f38a0eaf/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_body_3d.cpp#L1013-L1023
